title: Analogy drill
description: Twelve analogies at real pace, thirty seconds each. The ISEE has no analogies at all, so this is the format that exists only on the SSAT. The method never changes: say the relationship out loud as a sentence before you look at the choices.

questions.explanation: Say it first: a thermometer measures temperature. A clock measures time. A mirror reflects a face rather than measuring it, and that difference is the entire question.
A puppy is a young dog and a calf is a young cow. Choice A gets the young-of relationship right but changes species partway through, so it fails.

Famished is an extreme form of hungry, so the first word is the stronger one. Exhausted is an extreme form of tired, in that same order. Choice B has the right pair pointing the wrong way, and direction is what this question is testing.

A chef is the professional who works in a kitchen, and a judge is the professional who presides in a courtroom. A patient is in a hospital but does not work there, which is the distinction the wrong answers are built on.

Anonymous means without a name, and barefoot means without shoes. The relationship is the absence of a specific thing. Choice D is close, but an empty box lacks contents in general rather than one named thing.
Scissors are the tool used to cut, and a shovel is the tool used to dig. Choice C names a tool and the thing it acts on rather than the action, so it breaks the pattern.

A drop is one tiny unit of an enormous quantity of the same substance, and a grain is one tiny unit of sand. Choice C changes substance partway, since a page belongs to a book rather than directly to a library, and choice B is backwards.
You rehearse in preparation for a performance, and you train in preparation for a competition. Choice B happens after the event rather than before it, and timing is the relationship here.

A coward is defined by a lack of courage, and a miser is defined by a lack of generosity. Every other choice pairs a person with a quality they possess, which is exactly the opposite relationship. Whenever four choices share a pattern and one does not, the odd one is usually the answer.
Wood is the material you carve to shape it, and clay is the material you mold to shape it. Choice E is a material and something that happens to it accidentally, not a way of working it deliberately.

A symphony is the work created by a composer, and a novel is the work created by an author. Choice B is tempting, but a singer performs a song rather than necessarily writing it, and creating and performing are different relationships.

A dam stops the flow of a river, and a tourniquet stops the flow of blood. Choice B encloses rather than stops a flow, and choice D harnesses a flow instead of halting it. This is the hardest question here because the right answer comes from an unfamiliar subject, which is normal on the SSAT: the vocabulary is deliberately above grade level.
